entries.why_wrong: `price` is already declared right there in the parameter list — `calculateDiscount(price)` — so the function has access to it throughout the body. The actual problem is with `discount`, which is declared inside the `if` block and never escapes it, leaving the `return` line referencing a name that doesn't exist.

The multiplier itself is fine — `price * 0.1` correctly computes a 10% discount when that line actually runs. The bug isn't about the math being wrong, it's that `discount` is block-scoped to the `if` and unreachable on the `return` line, so the function throws before any multiplication result matters.

Adding an `else` wouldn't fix anything here — JavaScript doesn't require every `if` to have a matching `else`, and the code would run fine without one if `discount` were properly scoped. The real issue is that `const discount` is trapped inside the `if` block, so the unconditional `return price - discount` can't see it whether or not an `else` exists.
